newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian Hermis Bank yr profit to gain sharply.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian Hermis Bank yr profit to gain sharply.

text.p: One of Lithuania's leading banks, Hermis Bank, said it expected its net 1996 profit to be 25 million litas after 3.6 million litas profit in 1995.
"Our preliminary forecast, based on unaudited figures, is for a 1996 net profit of 25 million litas," Alexander Federas, director of the bank's international department, told Reuters on Monday.
Hermis, the second-largest private bank, was assigned a long-term senior debt rating of BB- and a short-term local currency debt rating of LC-2 by Thomson BankWatch on Friday.
Federas said that Hermis was pleased with the ratings but felt they were based on outdated figures.
"After our audited results for 1996 are made public at the end of March, we will apply to BankWatch for an upgrade," Federas said. The bank's unaudited results are due soon.
He added that the bank would also look for another rating this year, possibly from IBCA.
He also said that the bank was considering the possibility of a global depository receipt (GDR) issue this summer.
Its shareholders last week decided to boost its share capital by 23 million litas to 90 million litas.
Hermis Bank is 76 percent foreign owned and is one of the most active blue chip listings on Lithuania's bourse.
